[ADVISORY] app/models/post.rb:131-133 — cook_method == raw_html returns raw before the Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...) line, silently excluding raw-HTML posts from all registered plugin cook filters

[ADVISORY] app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:8-14 — Layout posts the resize message to the verbatim request.referer string, which may be absent or untrustworthy, causing postMessage to target an invalid origin so resizing silently never happens
[ADVISORY] config/locales/server.en.yml:1477 — The embed.permalink locale key is defined but unreferenced by any view, controller, or helper in this diff, leaving a dead translation string

[ADVISORY] TOCTOU race in TopicEmbed: where(embed_url: url).first followed by create!, with the 60s redis throttle inside the RetrieveTopic job, allows N concurrent jobs to pass the blank check; the loser crashes with ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique, and the embed page keeps reloading and re-enqueueing, generating a storm of failing jobs.

[ADVISORY] embed/loading.html.erb reloads unconditionally every 30 seconds with no terminal failure state; when retrieval fails the embed never transitions to content and every visitor loops reload→enqueue-job→fail forever with no bounded retry or error message.

[ADVISORY] Format drift on the join key: topic_id_for_embed compares the browser-supplied embed_url byte-for-byte against the stored RSS link, which may differ in trailing slash, query-param order, HTML-escaped ampersands, or case, causing missed lookups and duplicate topics/embed rows splitting the discussion; needs normalization at both write and read paths.

[ADVISORY] TopicRetriever runs Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) synchronously per missing embed URL, re-downloading and re-importing the whole feed N times in addition to the hourly scheduled job, causing O(articles × feed size) fetches and DB queries; should mark the URL for the next scheduled poll instead.

[ADVISORY] embed_controller referer check compares URI host case-sensitively against SiteSetting.embeddable_host, rejecting valid embeds from sites with mixed-case hosts; both sides should be normalized with host.downcase and embeddable_host validated on save.

[BUG] app/views/embed/best.html.erb:6 — '<%- end if %>' compiles to invalid Ruby (end if with no condition), causing a syntax error that 500s the entire success path of the embed feature

[BUG] app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:16 — 'if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }' uses substring matching instead of origin equality, allowing attacker pages whose URL contains the Discourse origin as a substring to pass the postMessage security check and drive iframe.height

[ADVISORY] lib/post_revisor.rb:85 — '@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])' changes PostRevisor's contract for all existing callers, silently skipping AR validations whenever skip_validations is passed, allowing invalid posts to be persisted

[ADVISORY] lib/tasks/disqus.thor:116 — removing the public -c/--category CLI option and replacing PostCreator with TopicEmbed.import_remote makes Disqus imports ignore the specified category and silently drop threads whose t[:link] is not an absolute http(s) URL

[ADVISORY] app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:11 — anonymous embeds enqueue Jobs::RetrieveTopic with user_id: current_user.try(:id), letting staff viewers bypass the 60s throttle for URLs unrelated to them, and every uncached embed request triggers a synchronous Jobs::PollFeed execution re-parsing the entire RSS feed — hot-path regression

[ADVISORY] app/views/embed/best.html.erb:20 — post.user.small_avatar_url / post.user.username dereference without a nil guard, causing NoMethodError and a permanent 500 on the embed iframe when the post's author was deleted

[ADVISORY] app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:14 — the loading path reloads every 30s while throttle/caching allow up to ~2 minutes of 'Loading Discussion…', and if retrieval legitimately fails the client reloads forever with no terminal error state

[BUG] Stored XSS: TopicEmbed.import creates posts with cook_method raw_html, and Post#cook returns raw content bypassing sanitization; RSS/scraped content with javascript: URLs in href/src survives into post.cooked and is rendered raw, executing attacker-controlled script in the forum origin.

[BUG] Attribute-context injection via unescaped url interpolated into a single-quoted href in the 'imported_from' footer in TopicEmbed (topic_embed.rb:11); url from params[:embed_url] can break out of the attribute causing stored XSS.

[ADVISORY] Referer is a client-controlled header used as the only gate for the embed endpoint, and TopicRetriever's host check compares only the host, not scheme/port/path, allowing forged Referer, arbitrary content fetching, port/scheme confusion, and unauthenticated enumeration of embedded topics' best posts.

[ADVISORY] Weak origin check on postMessage in embed.js uses substring-containment (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) instead of origin equality, letting a hostile parent whose origin is a substring of discourseUrl control iframe.height.

[ADVISORY] postMessage targetOrigin in embed.html.erb is taken from the client-controlled request.referer rendered into script, making the target origin attacker-influenced and causing resize postMessage to silently fail when mangled by escaping.
[ADVISORY] cook for raw_html posts bypasses Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...), silently disabling security/replacement plugin filters on imported embed posts.

[ADVISORY] spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:12-37 — every test stubs or mocks poll_feed and asserts only that it was called; none of the actual new logic in Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed (SimpleRSS.parse open, i.id fallback, CGI.unescapeHTML scrub massaging, TopicEmbed.import loop) is exercised, so regressions like raising on malformed feed items or nil URLs from broken i.id fallback pass the suite

[ADVISORY] spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:38-44 — the 'tells the topic retriever to work' test mocks TopicRetriever and asserts only the mock was called; it never asserts the 'loading' template was rendered, never checks enqueued job arguments, and the loading reload loop is verified by nothing

[ADVISORY] spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:8-10 — the 'is 404 without an embed_url' test asserts only response.should_not be_success, so it passes on any 4xx or 5xx including an unhandled NoMethodError; a regression making this path a 500 leaves the suite green while the stated 404 contract is violated

[ADVISORY] app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:1-27 — the entire client half of the feature (iframe construction, postMessage origin check, discourse-resize height handshake with layouts/embed.html.erb) has no tests anywhere in the diff; a change to the message type string or payload shape on either side of the cross-file protocol ships silently broken

[ADVISORY] spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb:36-44 — the update-path test asserts only post.cooked matches new contents and never verifies embed.content_sha1 was updated; if update_column(:content_sha1) is dropped or hashes the wrong string (pre-absolutized vs post-absolutized), every subsequent poll re-revises the post forever on the hourly PollFeed schedule

[BUG] db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3 adds `force: true` to `create_table :top_topics` in an already-shipped migration, so any re-run (db:migrate:redo, db:rollback + db:migrate, or replaying migration tool) executes `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS top_topics` first, destroying all top_topics rows with no backup, and the dropped data is unrecoverable

[ADVISORY] app/models/post.rb:131 reads `cook_method` unconditionally on every `cook` call, so any app server running the new code before the 20131219203905 migration has run crashes with `PGError: column posts.cook_method does not exist` on every post creation; code and migration must deploy atomically or a mixed deploy breaks all posting site-wide

[BUG] lib/tasks/disqus.thor:143 — the Disqus import rewrite to `TopicEmbed.import_remote` silently loses the original post timestamps (`created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at])` dropped), so imported topics are stamped with import time instead of the thread's real creation date
lib/tasks/disqus.thor:143 — the `-c/--category` option was removed from the CLI but `import_remote` always creates in the default category

lib/tasks/disqus.thor:143 — the deterministic permalink raw body is replaced by whatever readability scrapes from the live URL; if the page is unreachable or changed, `open(url)` raises and the thread is skipped entirely, so previously-importable Disqus data is no longer importable offline

[ADVISORY] app/models/topic_embed.rb:26 — no FK constraints or dependent-destroy on `topic_id`/`post_id`, so deleting the topic or post through the UI leaves an orphaned `topic_embeds` row; `TopicEmbed.import` then takes the update branch with `post == nil` and `PostRevisor.new(nil)` raises NoMethodError inside the PollFeed job, which has `retry: false`, so the feed poll dies mid-run and feed imports silently stall

[BUG] TopicEmbed.import returns nil silently when url is not an http(s) URL (also reached from PollFeed when i.id isn't http), with no log or error result; feed entries with non-http ids are silently dropped with success reported.

[BUG] SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) has no timeout, size cap, or error handling; errors inside the rss.items.each loop (e.g., item with no content element raising NoMethodError on nil.scrub, or PostCreator failure) abort all remaining items, and with retry: false the dropped entries are never retried.

[BUG] The throttle key retrieved:@embed_url is committed via $redis.setnx before the retrieve runs; if perform_retrieve no-ops or fails, the 60-second throttle still holds so retries return without doing work, and after expiry the same silent failure repeats indefinitely.

[ADVISORY] import_remote calls open(url).read with no timeout and no read-size cap on a path invoked from the retrieve_topic job and disqus thor task; a slow or huge remote page hangs the job worker indefinitely, draining worker capacity.

[ADVISORY] feed_key computes a 'feed-modified:<sha1>' cache key but nothing in the job reads or writes it — dead code from a dropped conditional-fetch optimization, so the job re-downloads and re-parses the entire feed every poll unconditionally.

[ADVISORY] When updating an existing embed whose post association is broken (post/topic deleted), PostRevisor.new(nil).revise! raises NoMethodError inside import, killing the whole feed-poll loop or retrieve_topic job rather than quarantining the stale embed row.

[ADVISORY] TopicView.new(topic_id, ...) in embed_controller is unguarded: if the topic_embed's topic was deleted, TopicView raises record-not-found and the endpoint returns a raw 500 instead of a 4xx/loading fallback.

[ADVISORY] The raise/rescue inside the ensure_embeddable before_filter means the X-Frame-Options header line is skipped on the error path, so error responses still carry Discourse's default SAMEORIGIN frame options and browsers refuse to render the 4xx error inside the embedding iframe.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:2 requires the wrong dependency 'jobs/regular/process_post' instead of 'jobs/scheduled/poll_feed', so the spec may not actually load Jobs::PollFeed, causing NameError in a focused rspec run

adjudication.rationale: In spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb the file explicitly does `require_dependency 'jobs/regular/process_post'` but the spec targets `Jobs::PollFeed` (a new class added at app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb). The spec does not require that poll_feed file, so in a focused/isolated run (where Rails autoload/eager-load doesn’t happen to load scheduled jobs) `Jobs::PollFeed` could be undefined, or the spec could inadvertently pass without actually loading the code under test.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] New gems ruby-readability and simple-rss added to the Gemfile but only Gemfile_rails4.lock was regenerated; other lockfiles like Gemfile.lock still lack the new dependencies, breaking bundle install --deployment and feed polling at deploy time

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `ruby-readability` and `simple-rss` to `Gemfile`, and updates `Gemfile_rails4.lock` to include them, but no other lockfiles are shown as updated in this PR. From the diff alone we can verify only that the Gemfile changed and only the rails4 lockfile was regenerated; whether this definitively breaks `bundle install --deployment` depends on the repo/deploy process and the presence/usage of other lockfiles (e.g., `Gemfile.lock`), which is not shown here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] poll_feed.rb:33 calls i.content.scrub without checking presence; Atom feeds commonly expose summary instead of content, so SimpleRSS returns nil and the hourly job raises NoMethodError, and with retry: false the feed poll silently dies every hour
String#scrub requires Ruby >= 2.1 but this codebase supports Ruby 1.9, so even valid content raises NoMethodError

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `i.content.scrub` in `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb` (`content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`). `String#scrub` is not available on older Rubies (e.g., Ruby 1.9), so if this app runs on Ruby 1.9 it would raise `NoMethodError` while polling feeds. The repo’s own comment in the Gemfile mentions Ruby 1.9 support (“perftools only works on 1.9 atm”), making this a verifiable compatibility defect introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] embed_controller.rb renders 'loading' view that reloads the page after 30 seconds, but topic creation happens in an async Sidekiq job with no guarantee of completion, leaving an infinite reload loop on failure path

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, when no existing embed is found it always enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` and renders `loading`. The `app/views/embed/loading.html.erb` page unconditionally does `setTimeout(function(){ document.location.reload(); }, 30000);`. If the Sidekiq job never creates a `TopicEmbed` (e.g., fetch failure, invalid `embed_url` host, or other permanent error), the controller will keep returning `loading` on each reload, causing an infinite reload loop and repeated job enqueues with no failure/stop condition shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] embed.css.scss requires ./vendor/normalize and ./common/foundation/base partials whose paths may drift from the main application manifest, causing Sprockets::FileNotFound at precompile time and breaking deployment

adjudication.rationale: The diff only shows a new stylesheet manifest (app/assets/stylesheets/embed.css.scss) with Sprockets requires to ./vendor/normalize and ./common/foundation/base, but it does not show whether those assets exist or whether embed.css.scss is added to the precompile list. The finding’s claim about “paths may drift” and causing Sprockets::FileNotFound at precompile time is speculative and not verifiable from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] topic_retriever.rb perform_retrieve invokes Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}) synchronously, re-fetching the entire RSS feed and performing TopicEmbed.import for every feed item per embedded page view; feed_key caching does not prevent repeats as it is never read or written

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve`, when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true it calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` synchronously (see `lib/topic_retriever.rb`), and `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` always fetches and iterates `rss.items` (see `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`). That can be a significant per-request performance/architecture concern (even though `retrieved_recently?` throttles per `@embed_url` to once per 60s, so it’s not literally every page view). Also, `Jobs::PollFeed#feed_key` is defined but never used (no reads/writes), so there is no caching mechanism in the diff to avoid repeated full-feed polling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] topic_embed.rb has a no-op require_dependency 'nokogiri' and inconsistent dependency loading for PostCreator/PostRevisor, relying on Rails autoload; direct console/rake use of TopicEmbed before full environment load fails with NameError

adjudication.rationale: In `app/models/topic_embed.rb` the file only does `require_dependency 'nokogiri'` but then directly references `PostCreator` and `PostRevisor` without any `require_dependency`/`require` of `post_creator` or `post_revisor` (those live in `lib/` per the diff). This does rely on Rails autoload/eager-load ordering to have those constants available, which is an inconsistency compared to other new code paths (e.g. `poll_feed.rb` explicitly `require_dependency 'post_creator'` and `post_revisor`). If the background retrieval never creates a `TopicEmbed` (e.g., fetch fails or `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` prevents retrieval), the client will reload forever. The finding’s general “reloads forever with no terminal error state” is directly supported by the diff (the “~2 minutes” detail is less directly evidenced).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Stored XSS: TopicEmbed.import creates posts with cook_method raw_html, and Post#cook returns raw content bypassing sanitization; RSS/scraped content with javascript: URLs in href/src survives into post.cooked and is rendered raw, executing attacker-controlled script in the forum origin.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new `cook_method` enum with `:raw_html` and changes `Post#cook` to `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, explicitly bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` from untrusted RSS/scraped HTML (`PollFeed` uses `SimpleRSS.parse open(...)` and `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`; `import_remote` uses Readability with allowed tags/attributes but no URL scheme sanitization shown). The helper `absolutize_urls` only rewrites relative `/...` links and does not strip/validate `javascript:` or other dangerous schemes in `href`/`src`. The embedded view renders `raw post.cooked`, and for `raw_html` posts `post.cooked == post.raw`, so attacker-controlled HTML/links can survive into rendered output on the forum origin, enabling stored XSS.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Attribute-context injection via unescaped url interpolated into a single-quoted href in the 'imported_from' footer in TopicEmbed (topic_embed.rb:11); url from params[:embed_url] can break out of the attribute causing stored XSS.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, untrusted `url` is interpolated directly into an HTML attribute using single quotes: `"#{url}"` and appended to `contents`. The only validation is `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which still allows characters like `'` to break out of the `href` attribute (e.g., `http://a.com/' onmouseover='...`). This content is then stored as a post with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and later rendered with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` in `app/views/embed/best.html.erb`, making stored XSS feasible. The URL can originate from `params[:embed_url]` via `RetrieveTopic`/`TopicRetriever` or from RSS items in `PollFeed`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Referer is a client-controlled header used as the only gate for the embed endpoint, and TopicRetriever's host check compares only the host, not scheme/port/path, allowing forged Referer, arbitrary content fetching, port/scheme confusion, and unauthenticated enumeration of embedded topics' best posts.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces an embed endpoint (`EmbedController#best`) whose only access control is `ensure_embeddable`, which validates solely `URI(request.referer).host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host` and then sets `X-Frame-Options = ALLOWALL`. Since `Referer` is client-controlled, a non-browser client can forge it to pass this gate. Additionally, `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` checks only `URI(@embed_url).host` against `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, ignoring scheme/port, so URLs like `http://allowedhost:1234/...` will pass and later be fetched via `open(url)` in `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, enabling unintended port/scheme access. The endpoint is otherwise unauthenticated and will render topic highlights when an embed exists (`TopicView.new(... {best: 5})`), allowing enumeration by probing `embed_url` values.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Weak origin check on postMessage in embed.js uses substring-containment (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) instead of origin equality, letting a hostile parent whose origin is a substring of discourseUrl control iframe.height.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js`, the message handler accepts postMessages if `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) !== -1`. This is a substring containment check rather than validating that `e.origin` equals the expected Discourse origin (scheme/host/port). As written, any origin that is a substring of `discourseUrl` would pass the check and could send `{type:'discourse-resize', height: ...}` to control `iframe.height`, which is a security/correctness issue introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] postMessage targetOrigin in embed.html.erb is taken from the client-controlled request.referer rendered into script, making the target origin attacker-influenced and causing resize postMessage to silently fail when mangled by escaping.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb`, the iframe sends `parent.postMessage(..., '<%= request.referer %>')`. `targetOrigin` must be an origin (scheme+host+port), not a full URL; `request.referer` will typically include a path/query, so the postMessage can fail/throw and resizing may not work. Additionally, Rails will HTML-escape the interpolated referer inside the JS string, potentially mangling characters (e.g., `&` -> `&`) and further increasing the chance of silent mismatch/failure. Although `ensure_embeddable` validates the referer host, it doesn’t ensure `targetOrigin` is a valid origin string for postMessage.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] cook for raw_html posts bypasses Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...), silently disabling security/replacement plugin filters on imported embed posts.

adjudication.rationale: In app/models/post.rb, Post#cook now returns `raw` immediately when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, which bypasses the normal cooking pipeline including `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)`. The diff also introduces RSS/import paths that explicitly set `cook_method: :raw_html` (TopicEmbed.import via PostCreator), so imported/embed posts will skip all after-cook plugin filters (including any security/sanitization/replacement done there) by design of this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:12-37 — every test stubs or mocks poll_feed and asserts only that it was called; none of the actual new logic in Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed (SimpleRSS.parse open, i.id fallback, CGI.unescapeHTML scrub massaging, TopicEmbed.import loop) is exercised, so regressions like raising on malformed feed items or nil URLs from broken i.id fallback pass the suite

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds substantial logic in `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` (requiring `simple-rss`, `SimpleRSS.parse open(...)`, iterating `rss.items`, URL fallback to `i.id`, `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`, and calling `TopicEmbed.import`). However, `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb` only tests `execute`’s gating and delegates by mocking/stubbing `poll_feed` (e.g., `poller.expects(:poll_feed).never/once`) and never exercises `poll_feed` itself. This leaves the new parsing/import behavior untested and susceptible to regressions without failing specs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb:33-43 — 'valid host' tests stub retrieved_recently? and mock perform_retrieve, so the Redis throttle logic (setnx/expire, no_throttle staff bypass), the TopicEmbed-already-exists race guard, and the feed_polling_enabled? → Jobs::PollFeed dispatch path have zero coverage; a regression dropping the setnx check turns every anonymous page view into a remote HTTP fetch with no failing test

adjudication.rationale: In spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb, the “valid host” examples explicitly stub TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently? (returns true/false) and only assert whether #perform_retrieve is called, without exercising the real Redis throttling path in TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently? (the $redis.setnx/expire logic and @opts[:no_throttle] bypass). The spec also never exercises TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve’s internal branches (TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: ...).exists? early return, feed_polling_enabled? → Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute, and subsequent fetch_http/TopicEmbed.import_remote). This is a concrete coverage gap for newly added nontrivial behavior, not a verifiable functional defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:38-44 — the 'tells the topic retriever to work' test mocks TopicRetriever and asserts only the mock was called; it never asserts the 'loading' template was rendered, never checks enqueued job arguments, and the loading reload loop is verified by nothing

adjudication.rationale: The finding is grounded: in spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb the test "tells the topic retriever to work when no previous embed is found" only asserts calls on a mocked TopicRetriever and does not assert the controller’s actual behavior when topic_id is nil. In the diff, EmbedController#best enqueues Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...) and renders 'loading' (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb), it does not call TopicRetriever directly. The spec also does not verify rendering of the loading template or the enqueue arguments, so the test is both incomplete and misaligned with the implementation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:8-10 — the 'is 404 without an embed_url' test asserts only response.should_not be_success, so it passes on any 4xx or 5xx including an unhandled NoMethodError; a regression making this path a 500 leaves the suite green while the stated 404 contract is violated

adjudication.rationale: In spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb the example named "is 404 without an embed_url" only asserts `response.should_not be_success` after `get :best`. Given the controller uses `params.require(:embed_url)` (EmbedController#best), that path could return various non-success statuses (e.g., 400 from ParameterMissing) or even a 500 if an unhandled exception occurs, and the test would still pass, so it does not actually enforce the stated 404 contract.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:1-27 — the entire client half of the feature (iframe construction, postMessage origin check, discourse-resize height handshake with layouts/embed.html.erb) has no tests anywhere in the diff; a change to the message type string or payload shape on either side of the cross-file protocol ships silently broken

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a cross-file client/server postMessage protocol: app/assets/javascripts/embed.js listens for `message` events and expects `e.data.type === 'discourse-resize'` with a `height`, while app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb sends `parent.postMessage({type: 'discourse-resize', height: ...}, '<%= request.referer %>')`. The added specs cover controller/model/job behavior (e.g., EmbedController, TopicRetriever, PollFeed, TopicEmbed) but introduce no tests for the JS iframe/embed handshake or the message payload/type coupling, so a change to the string or shape could break embedding without test detection.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb:36-44 — the update-path test asserts only post.cooked matches new contents and never verifies embed.content_sha1 was updated; if update_column(:content_sha1) is dropped or hashes the wrong string (pre-absolutized vs post-absolutized), every subsequent poll re-revises the post forever on the hourly PollFeed schedule

adjudication.rationale: In spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb the “Supports updating the post” example only asserts that `post.cooked` reflects the new contents, and does not assert that the associated `TopicEmbed` row’s `content_sha1` was updated. In the implementation, the update path relies on `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)` inside `TopicEmbed.import` to prevent repeated revisions when the feed content is unchanged. The finding correctly identifies a specific, diff-grounded test gap around this nontrivial control logic (avoiding unnecessary re-revisions on subsequent polls).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3 adds `force: true` to `create_table :top_topics` in an already-shipped migration, so any re-run (db:migrate:redo, db:rollback + db:migrate, or replaying migration tool) executes `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS top_topics` first, destroying all top_topics rows with no backup, and the dropped data is unrecoverable

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change an existing (timestamped) migration to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`, which in Rails will drop the table if it already exists when that migration is executed. However, for an already-migrated production DB, Rails will not re-run this migration during normal `db:migrate`, so this does not introduce an immediate, verifiable runtime defect from the diff alone. It is still a concrete, diff-grounded risk/maintenance issue because modifying an old migration and adding `force: true` increases the chance of unexpected data loss if the migration is ever replayed on a DB where `top_topics` exists (e.g., via nonstandard migration replay tooling).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb:2 uses `force: true` on a brand-new table, which is unnecessary, establishes a destructive pattern, and if the migration is replayed after data exists existing topic_embed rows and their links to imported topics are silently dropped, leaving orphaned topics that can never be re-linked via the embed URL lookup

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateTopicEmbeds` does use `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true` (new file `db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb`). For a brand-new table this is unnecessary and sets a risky/destructive precedent since `force: true` drops an existing table if present. However, based on the diff alone, Rails migrations are normally not replayed once applied (tracked via `schema_migrations`), so the claimed real-world data loss/orphaning scenario is speculative and not directly verifiable as an introduced defect from this PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] app/models/post.rb:131 reads `cook_method` unconditionally on every `cook` call, so any app server running the new code before the 20131219203905 migration has run crashes with `PGError: column posts.cook_method does not exist` on every post creation; code and migration must deploy atomically or a mixed deploy breaks all posting site-wide

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new `posts.cook_method` column via migration `20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb`, and also adds `Post#cook` logic that reads `cook_method` on every call (`return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` in `app/models/post.rb`). If application code is deployed before the migration has run (mixed/rolling deploy), the `cook_method` attribute/method won’t exist on `Post` according to the pre-migration schema, causing runtime exceptions when `cook` is invoked (likely `NoMethodError`/missing attribute rather than the exact `PGError` cited). This is a real deploy-order break introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] lib/tasks/disqus.thor:143 — the Disqus import rewrite to `TopicEmbed.import_remote` silently loses the original post timestamps (`created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at])` dropped), so imported topics are stamped with import time instead of the thread's real creation date

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/tasks/disqus.thor`, the previous `PostCreator.new(... created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]) ...)` was removed and replaced with `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`. `TopicEmbed.import_remote` only uses `opts[:title]` and `TopicEmbed.import` calls `PostCreator.new` without any `created_at` option, so the created post/topic will default to import time rather than the Disqus thread’s original `created_at`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:143 — the `-c/--category` option was removed from the CLI but `import_remote` always creates in the default category

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly removes the `-c/--category` option from `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` (deleted `method_option :category` and all `category_id` handling) and replaces topic creation with `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`. `TopicEmbed.import_remote`/`.import` ultimately calls `PostCreator.new(user, title: ..., raw: ..., ...)` without any category parameter, so the CLI can no longer control category and will fall back to whatever default `PostCreator` uses. This is a real, diff-grounded behavioral regression/feature removal, but not provably an internal correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/tasks/disqus.thor:143 — the deterministic permalink raw body is replaced by whatever readability scrapes from the live URL; if the page is unreachable or changed, `open(url)` raises and the thread is skipped entirely, so previously-importable Disqus data is no longer importable offline

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/tasks/disqus.thor`, the import path was changed from creating a post with deterministic raw content (a permalink built from `t[:link]`) to `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`. `TopicEmbed.import_remote` calls `open(url).read` with no error handling; if the URL is unreachable/changed/returns an error, this will raise and can abort the import (or at least prevent that thread from being imported). This introduces a network dependency and can make previously-offline Disqus imports fail, matching the finding’s concern about regressions in importability.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] app/models/topic_embed.rb:26 — no FK constraints or dependent-destroy on `topic_id`/`post_id`, so deleting the topic or post through the UI leaves an orphaned `topic_embeds` row; `TopicEmbed.import` then takes the update branch with `post == nil` and `PostRevisor.new(nil)` raises NoMethodError inside the PollFeed job, which has `retry: false`, so the feed poll dies mid-run and feed imports silently stall

adjudication.rationale: `topic_embeds` is introduced with `topic_id`/`post_id` columns but no FK constraints and `TopicEmbed` has no `dependent:` behavior on its `belongs_to :topic` / `belongs_to :post`. In `TopicEmbed.import`, the update branch does `post = embed.post` and then unconditionally `PostRevisor.new(post)` when the content hash changes; if the associated post was deleted (leaving an orphaned `topic_embeds` row), `embed.post` can be `nil` and this will raise. `Jobs::PollFeed` calls `TopicEmbed.import(...)` inside an `rss.items.each` loop and is configured with `sidekiq_options retry: false`, so an exception mid-run would stop processing further items and not be retried.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] When the enqueued retrieve_topic job fails to produce an embed (embed_by_username unset, user doesn't exist, TopicRetriever#fetch_http silently returns nil), the controller returns the loading page which reloads every 30s forever — failure is invisible to the end user and no topic is ever created.

adjudication.rationale: Verified in diff: `EmbedController#best` renders `loading` when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` is nil and enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb). The loading view auto-reloads every 30s (app/views/embed/loading.html.erb). If the job can’t create an embed, this loop never resolves. In `TopicRetriever#fetch_http`, it returns early when the configured posting user can’t be found (`return if user.blank?`), so no `TopicEmbed` is created and the controller will keep serving the loading page on every reload. Additionally, if `SiteSetting.embed_by_username` is nil, `downcase` will raise, causing the job to fail and still leaving the user stuck on the reload loop. No error is surfaced to the end user in either case.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] TopicEmbed.import returns nil silently when url is not an http(s) URL (also reached from PollFeed when i.id isn't http), with no log or error result; feed entries with non-http ids are silently dropped with success reported.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the first line `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//` causes a silent `nil` return for any non-http(s) URL. `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` explicitly falls back to `i.id` when `i.link` is blank or not http(s): `url = i.id if url.blank? || url !~ /^https?\:\/\//`, and then calls `TopicEmbed.import(user, url, ...)`. If the feed’s `id`/GUID is non-http(s) (a common RSS/Atom case), the item will be skipped with no logging/error signaling in this code path, so entries can be silently dropped.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) has no timeout, size cap, or error handling; errors inside the rss.items.each loop (e.g., item with no content element raising NoMethodError on nil.scrub, or PostCreator failure) abort all remaining items, and with retry: false the dropped entries are never retried.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the job does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` with no timeout/size cap and no `rescue`, so network hangs or parse/open errors will raise and abort the job. Inside the loop it does `i.content.scrub` without guarding `i.content` (if `content` is nil this will raise `NoMethodError`), which would stop processing remaining items. The job sets `sidekiq_options retry: false`, so failures won’t be retried by Sidekiq (and a mid-loop exception prevents remaining items from being imported in that run).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The throttle key retrieved:@embed_url is committed via $redis.setnx before the retrieve runs; if perform_retrieve no-ops or fails, the 60-second throttle still holds so retries return without doing work, and after expiry the same silent failure repeats indefinitely.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?`, the code sets the Redis throttle key (`retrieved:#{@embed_url}`) via `$redis.setnx` and `$redis.expire(..., 60)` before `perform_retrieve` is executed (`retrieve` calls `perform_retrieve` unless `retrieved_recently?`). If `perform_retrieve` later returns early (e.g., `fetch_http` returns when `embed_by_username` user is blank) or raises during the HTTP fetch/import, subsequent calls within 60 seconds will be skipped even though no embed was created. This is a real robustness/retry-semantics concern grounded in the diff, but it’s not a clearly verifiable “broken behavior” since a 60s backoff may be intentional.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] import_remote calls open(url).read with no timeout and no read-size cap on a path invoked from the retrieve_topic job and disqus thor task; a slow or huge remote page hangs the job worker indefinitely, draining worker capacity.

adjudication.rationale: TopicEmbed.import_remote does `open(url).read` (open-uri) with no explicit open/read timeouts and no limit on bytes read. This method is invoked from TopicRetriever#fetch_http (used by Jobs::RetrieveTopic) and from the Disqus thor task (`TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], ...)`). A slow/unresponsive host or very large response can block the job/thread indefinitely and/or consume excessive memory, reducing worker capacity (availability defect).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] feed_key computes a 'feed-modified:<sha1>' cache key but nothing in the job reads or writes it — dead code from a dropped conditional-fetch optimization, so the job re-downloads and re-parses the entire feed every poll unconditionally.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the method `feed_key` computes a Redis-style cache key (`"feed-modified:<sha1>"`) but nothing in this job (or in the shown diff) ever calls `feed_key` or reads/writes any value keyed by it. The job unconditionally does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` on every run, so the observation about dead/unused code and unconditional re-download/re-parse is grounded. This is an inefficiency/cleanup concern rather than a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] When updating an existing embed whose post association is broken (post/topic deleted), PostRevisor.new(nil).revise! raises NoMethodError inside import, killing the whole feed-poll loop or retrieve_topic job rather than quarantining the stale embed row.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, when an embed row already exists it does `post = embed.post` and, if the content hash changed, unconditionally runs `revisor = PostRevisor.new(post)` then `revisor.revise!(...)`. If the associated post/topic has been deleted (broken association), `embed.post` will be `nil`, and `PostRevisor` methods will dereference `@post` (set from `nil`) leading to a `NoMethodError`. There is no guard/rescue here, so the scheduled feed poll (`Jobs::PollFeed`) loop or `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` execution can be killed by a stale `topic_embeds` row.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] TopicView.new(topic_id, ...) in embed_controller is unguarded: if the topic_embed's topic was deleted, TopicView raises record-not-found and the endpoint returns a raw 500 instead of a 4xx/loading fallback.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` returns a `topic_id`, the code unconditionally does `TopicView.new(topic_id, current_user, {best: 5})` with no rescue/fallback. The `topic_embeds` table has no FK constraints and no `dependent:` cleanup is shown, so it’s possible for a `TopicEmbed` row to remain after its `Topic` is deleted. In that case, `TopicView.new` (or subsequent uses of `@topic_view.topic` in the view) can raise record-not-found, yielding a 500 instead of rendering `loading` or a 4xx.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The raise/rescue inside the ensure_embeddable before_filter means the X-Frame-Options header line is skipped on the error path, so error responses still carry Discourse's default SAMEORIGIN frame options and browsers refuse to render the 4xx error inside the embedding iframe.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable`, `response.headers['X-Frame-Options'] = "ALLOWALL"` is only set after the host/referer checks pass. On the error paths (`embeddable_host.blank?`, referer host mismatch, or `URI::InvalidURIError`), the method raises before setting the header, so error responses from `/embed/best` will not get the explicit `ALLOWALL` header added by this controller. Whether Discourse adds a default `SAMEORIGIN` (and thus blocks rendering the error in an iframe) is not shown in this diff, so that consequence can’t be fully verified here, but the header omission on error is real and diff-grounded.
